season_garden_02_001.speaker: narrator
season_garden_02_001.text: The second garden afternoon began with sunlight on the wet doorstep and a smell of sawn timber from the work area. Yue arrived after eating at home, which made the room feel less like a question she had to answer quickly. She set her bag down, checked the agreed start time and asked whether any safety notice had changed since the first visit. The upper damaged path remained closed. Staff had cleared the side entrance and kept the permitted route in use.

season_garden_02_002.speaker: rival_qiu_zhen
season_garden_02_002.text: Qiu arrived carrying no extra materials. She had once planned to bring spare copper wire from her own kit, then decided that an unrequested donation would confuse both the design and the account. She told Yue this as they washed their hands. “I am trying to stop rescuing a task before it has asked for the thing I happen to own,” she said. “The wire would have made a very fine excuse to use the gauge. The actual job wants sound timber.”

season_garden_02_003.speaker: narrator
season_garden_02_003.text: The gardener met them beside the light work table. The first priority recorded on their earlier page would govern the assigned preparation; its unchosen companion request retained the later agreed session. All heavy cutting and fitting remained with the responsible workers. Neither helper had earned another wage by thinking about the orchard at home. Yue liked the fact that her unfinished thoughts could arrive without becoming unpaid hours. Qiu inspected the prepared pieces and waited for the actual instructions before touching them.

season_garden_02_004.speaker: narrator
season_garden_02_004.text: The work began with the priority their saved choice had actually selected. Yue carried its immediate result only as far as the staff had confirmed it. A completed light piece was a completed light piece; an installed section, checked bench or permitted route would require its own later action. They had time before the scheduled break to finish the first preparation, ask the responsible worker to examine it and correct what that examination found. The clock on the wall moved without demanding that they imitate it.

season_garden_02_005.speaker: narrator
season_garden_02_005.text: After the first preparation, both women washed timber dust from their fingers. Yue found a narrow pale line where her hand had gripped the tool too tightly. It was not an injury, but it told her something about the way she had been trying to make light work feel decisive. Qiu flexed her own fingers. The two women drank from cups filled at the ordinary kitchen supply, whose afternoon amount had been set aside by staff. Nobody drew water through a cultivation circuit.

season_garden_02_006.speaker: lin_yue
season_garden_02_006.text: “I caught myself holding my breath when I checked the edge,” Yue said. “As if I could make a crooked line less crooked by refusing to breathe.” Qiu answered that she sometimes did the same while timing a closure. The familiar habit did not turn a table task into a safe practice demonstration. Yue put the gauge down before trying a calmer grip. Her registered Four pairs remained a bounded capacity she owned; it was not a reason to use qi whenever the work resisted her hands.

season_garden_02_007.speaker: narrator
season_garden_02_007.text: From the healing hall came a muffled argument. A patient wanted to leave before the next clinical check because somebody expected her at a household shop. Ren Qiao did not discuss her diagnosis across the doorway. He asked to speak in the private room, then arranged for an authorized staff member to help contact the person she named. Yue and Qiu continued cleaning their table. The patient's life beyond the orchard was real even while its private details remained unavailable to the helpers.

season_garden_02_008.speaker: narrator
season_garden_02_008.text: Qiu paused when the patient's voice rose again. The sentence she heard was that rest did not sell anything. Her jaw tightened in recognition. Yue asked whether she wanted to move their table farther from the doorway so their work would not become an audience. Qiu agreed. Staff approved the new light-table position, and the women shifted its empty removable trays rather than lift the table themselves. A small change in work placement made less of somebody else's difficult afternoon visible to strangers.

season_garden_02_009.speaker: rival_qiu_zhen
season_garden_02_009.text: “I have said something like that,” Qiu admitted. “Not here. Somewhere I did not have enough money to make stopping feel like a simple instruction.” She picked a splinter from a waste piece, then put it down when she saw Yue looking. “I do not need you to solve the sentence for me. I just disliked hearing it as if it were foolish.” Yue said she had not thought it foolish. Good advice still had to find a life in which it could be followed.

season_garden_02_010.speaker: narrator
season_garden_02_010.text: They spoke about wages while the corrected pieces dried under the carpenter's instruction. Three copper for three completed hours would not answer every cost the patient's household faced. The garden reserve did not pretend to do so. Its arrangement could still avoid making a helper prove pain before taking an agreed break, or trade tomorrow's strength for an extra visible finish today. Qiu said that a small fair rule could be worth keeping without naming it a rescue. Yue agreed and checked her own break time.

season_garden_02_011.speaker: narrator
season_garden_02_011.text: The pinwheel child returned with his grandmother, this time on a visit arranged by the clinical staff within her current plan. She did not walk farther because she had enjoyed the previous visit. Her support and accompanying staff member remained appropriate to that day's assessment. The child asked if the pinwheel could be hung closer to her chair. Staff and grandmother checked the new low position. He moved it himself while Yue held the bag open, careful not to decide that a cheerful object made the chair unnecessary.

season_garden_02_012.speaker: narrator
season_garden_02_012.text: The grandmother wanted to tell Yue how tall she had been when she planted her first bean. She held her hand beside her knee, then laughed because the child thought beans must have been enormous in those days. The story had a young self inside it that Yue could not see in the tired woman before her. For a moment the garden stopped looking like a place divided into helpers and patients. It held people who had done all kinds of things before arriving with today's limits.

season_garden_02_013.speaker: lin_yue
season_garden_02_013.text: “Did it grow well?” Yue asked. The grandmother said the first bean had died because she had watered it whenever she worried. Her older sister had then given her a second one and an instruction to leave it alone long enough to put down roots. The child thought this meant worrying killed plants. His grandmother corrected him: too much water had killed that particular plant. Worry had merely been the reason her small hands kept pouring. Yue appreciated the precision more than a tidy lesson.

season_garden_02_014.speaker: narrator
season_garden_02_014.text: Qiu brought a dry saucer at the woman's request. She asked whether the child wanted to keep the pinwheel string out of the cup, since the wind kept dropping it toward the water. He rearranged the knot and tested it with solemn care. A fast practical answer did something useful here. Yue watched Qiu's face soften at his satisfaction. The quick closing method was not on display, but the interest that had made it mattered: Qiu wanted things to work soon enough for an actual person.

season_garden_02_015.speaker: narrator
season_garden_02_015.text: When the grandmother tired, the staff member accompanied her back along the permitted route. The child asked Yue whether she could stay outside for him. Yue said she had work in the hall and asked who was responsible for his next activity. His visiting adult called from the doorway. The child went there without a dramatic farewell. Yue had offered useful attention without silently accepting child care for the rest of the afternoon. Her own three-hour session still had a beginning, a purpose and an end.

season_garden_02_016.speaker: narrator
season_garden_02_016.text: The gardener then brought a tray of damaged plant labels. This was light table work already within the helpers' agreed assignment. Staff had identified the plants corresponding to two readable markers and left several others unresolved. The women could copy confirmed names onto new labels under instruction; they could not identify medicine by resemblance or create doses from a fading name. Qiu asked which ink would survive weather. The gardener supplied the approved ink and explained when the labels could be placed after drying.

season_garden_02_017.speaker: narrator
season_garden_02_017.text: Yue's handwriting looked awkward beside Qiu's. She usually wrote small, packing a page with every qualification she feared somebody might otherwise miss. These labels needed to be read from a standing position by the people doing the actual work. Qiu offered a spare ruled guide, then asked whether Yue wanted it. Yue did. She enlarged the letters and left the approved spacing between names. The guide made the work easier without making her hand belong to the person who had supplied it.

season_garden_02_018.speaker: narrator
season_garden_02_018.text: One confirmed plant had a common name that sounded like a promised cure. Yue asked Ren Qiao whether the garden should use the dispenser's exact stock name instead. He said the gardener and apothecary would decide the label for their own stock; clinical staff already used the correct identifiers in treatment. He agreed that a poetic name could invite a mistaken claim, then declined to turn every garden conversation into a medicine lecture. The women took the naming question to the responsible gardener.

season_garden_02_019.speaker: ren_qiao
season_garden_02_019.text: “People need ordinary ways to enjoy plants,” Ren said before leaving. “I would rather they knew which questions belong to treatment than thought beauty itself dangerous. You can tell a visitor that you like a flower. You cannot tell them it will mend their shoulder because it grows near our hall.” Yue smiled at the pointed example. Her injury had made every root look tempting on difficult mornings. Wanting relief did not supply evidence that a particular plant could provide it.

season_garden_02_020.speaker: narrator
season_garden_02_020.text: A woman visiting the apothecary asked whether the fresh labels meant a new harvest was ready. The gardener said the bed had suffered damage and no increased supply was being promised. Existing stock remained subject to the ordinary dispensing process and actual quantities. The woman sighed and said she had hoped to avoid another trip. Qiu asked whether staff could tell her when confirmed availability would next be known. That question did not create medicine, but it could spare an unnecessary journey.

season_garden_02_021.speaker: narrator
season_garden_02_021.text: The answer was an ordinary date after the scheduled stock check, with contact arrangements handled by the apothecary and only for people who wanted them. Yue saw the visiting woman relax a little without receiving the thing she had first wanted. Qiu returned to the label table. “That was faster than telling her ten reasons the plants aren't ready,” she said. Yue agreed, then added that the date should change if the stock check was delayed. Qiu made an exasperated face and nodded.

season_garden_02_022.speaker: narrator
season_garden_02_022.text: The disagreement had begun to acquire humor without becoming harmless. Both women knew there were circumstances where a delay cost more than irritation. Qiu had seen quick work dismissed before anyone measured what the waiting itself consumed. Yue had learned that a clean end to a visible action could hide a body still paying for it. The garden offered no single dial to settle them. It offered different people, different costs and an afternoon short enough that a useful choice would leave something undone.

season_garden_02_023.speaker: narrator
season_garden_02_023.text: At the next break, Yue used the chair with a back again. Her shoulder felt tired without the sharper line from the first visit. She described that ordinary state only as much as work planning required. Her clinical questions stayed for the clinician she would consult if the condition changed. Qiu walked to the doorway and stood in the sunlight, then returned to sit. The gardener asked if she needed another assignment. She said she needed her scheduled break. The sentence seemed to surprise them both.

season_garden_02_024.speaker: rival_qiu_zhen
season_garden_02_024.text: “I almost asked for something to do while you rested,” Qiu told Yue. “Then I realized I was resting too. If I make my break into a little extra job, somebody may begin to expect it. Worse, I may begin to expect it.” She loosened the cord at her wrist. Yue said she had once felt that putting down a tool was a way of confessing she was replaceable. Qiu looked toward the table. “We are replaceable at many tasks. That needn't be an insult.”

season_garden_02_025.speaker: narrator
season_garden_02_025.text: A kitchen worker passed carrying a covered tray. She was glad the helpers had moved their work away from the patient doorway because people carrying food could now turn without brushing wet labels. The change had produced another useful consequence neither woman had planned. Yue resisted writing it as proof that all courtesy improved efficiency. Sometimes a courteous change helped a task, and sometimes it cost time for a reason still worth choosing. This one simply gave the worker an easier turn.

season_garden_02_026.speaker: narrator
season_garden_02_026.text: The work table's new position also caught brighter light. Qiu noticed a flaw in a piece she had earlier marked ready. She called the carpenter before adding it to the accepted stack. He examined the grain and rejected that piece for the intended fitting, approving a replacement from existing sound stock. Qiu's quick preparation had not made the flaw; her later attention had caught it. Yue said that aloud after the carpenter left. Qiu answered that she knew, then looked relieved to hear it anyway.

season_garden_02_027.speaker: narrator
season_garden_02_027.text: They had one hour remaining. The carpenter gave each helper a limited correction that could be completed without heavy force: a smoother edge on a removable light piece and a clearer mark on an orientation line. Qiu reached for the tool, stopped and checked which hand movement the instruction required. Yue changed the angle of her tray so her shoulder could remain supported. Neither adjustment looked impressive. Both made the actual task more likely to remain within the afternoon rather than follow their bodies home.

season_garden_02_028.speaker: narrator
season_garden_02_028.text: Outside, a wind gust swept loose blossoms from the intact plum across the permitted path. A visitor said the tree was shedding its strength. The gardener answered that fallen blossoms did not describe an illness without other evidence. Qiu watched a petal catch on her boot. She lifted it with the side of a finger and placed it on the sill, then seemed embarrassed by the useless action. Yue did not ask it to become a symbol. A petal could simply be something somebody preferred not to tread on.

season_garden_02_029.speaker: lin_yue
season_garden_02_029.text: “Have you always liked gardens?” Yue asked. Qiu said no; she liked working places where people could point to something and tell her what it was supposed to do. Gardens kept hiding half the process beneath soil. Yue laughed and said that sounded like a reason to like them. Qiu gave her a skeptical look. Their differences reached beyond the measured method. A rival could be somebody whose impatience revealed a question Yue had been willing to leave unasked for too long.

season_garden_02_030.speaker: narrator
season_garden_02_030.text: Qiu said that when her sister came, they often walked through market plant stalls and disagreed over what would survive on a small windowsill. Her sister chose by flower color; Qiu asked about drainage until the sellers began answering the sister instead. Yue did not infer that Qiu's family made every home easy. The story told her only about those visits and those stalls. She asked what the sister would choose for this court. Qiu said something bright enough to be seen from indoors.

season_garden_02_031.speaker: narrator
season_garden_02_031.text: The kitchen woman came to collect the carpenter's current bench update. Depending on the selected priority, preparation had either made the seating fittings ready for his confirmed return or left them at their retained next session while the route border progressed. Su and the worker gave her the actual status, not a generic promise that everything was nearly finished. The woman wanted to know whether she should move her little carved rail to another shelf. That decision did not depend on the helpers making the faster-looking choice.

season_garden_02_032.speaker: narrator
season_garden_02_032.text: Yue followed her into the dining hall while Qiu completed her own assigned correction. The old rail was resting on a folded cloth beside a bowl of dry beans. The woman touched the bird and said she kept remembering her husband's irritation at the bad wings. She had not spoken about his final illness. Yue did not ask for that larger sorrow as the price of taking the smaller memory seriously. They talked about whether a little shelf could keep the rail away from spilled water.

season_garden_02_033.speaker: narrator
season_garden_02_033.text: Staff confirmed that the existing shelf could hold the light keepsake, and the owner placed it herself. Yue offered no structural work outside her assignment. The bird sat crookedly against the wall, half hidden by the beans. Its awkwardness looked at home. When the woman said she should perhaps have asked for it to be straightened, Yue asked whether she wanted that now. She said no. Her preference did not need to remain consistent with the way a visitor expected a memorial to look.

season_garden_02_034.speaker: narrator
season_garden_02_034.text: Back at the work table, Qiu had finished the requested correction and was waiting for the qualified check. She did not start another unagreed task to make the waiting disappear. Yue reported only that the keepsake had a shelf; she did not repeat the owner's private grief. Qiu asked whether the bird had flown at last. Yue said it was among beans. Qiu laughed, a short surprised sound that made the afternoon feel more ordinary than the word memorial had allowed.

season_garden_02_035.speaker: narrator
season_garden_02_035.text: The carpenter accepted the corrected light pieces and retained responsibility for final installation, inspection and the permitted use of their assemblies. The gardener took the confirmed labels after their ink had dried. Yue counted the unresolved markers still remaining in the doubtful crock. They were fewer than before and still unresolved. A work report could hold both facts without calling the garden repaired. Qiu wiped the bronze gauge with a dry cloth and checked that it was her own instrument before returning it to her bag.

season_garden_02_036.speaker: narrator
season_garden_02_036.text: Su asked each helper whether the accepted assignment had stayed within the agreed hours and limits. Yue described the light corrections, the label work and the time spent waiting for the checks. Qiu described the rejected piece and its sound replacement. Neither concealed the correction to make the first preparation look flawless. The report recorded completed work and the responsible owners of unfinished installation. Su asked what should change next session. Yue said the light was better at the new table position, if the doorway could remain clear.

season_garden_02_037.speaker: rival_su_yao
season_garden_02_037.text: “We can keep a useful change provisionally,” Su said. “If patient access or food delivery later needs this space, the table moves again. Nobody owns a convenient spot because it worked once.” Qiu said she liked the word provisionally less every time it appeared. Su smiled. “Then you may name the conditions exactly. We will still have to live with their ability to change.” Yue saw Qiu consider a retort, decide against it and make the more useful note about the doorway.

season_garden_02_038.speaker: narrator
season_garden_02_038.text: The day's materials record contained no new purchase. Existing approved stock had covered the light preparation and replacement; the bench's separate authorized six-copper repair remained with the carpenter's actual completion. Forty copper had been reserved for materials, not declared spent merely because a list existed. Each helper had completed another three-hour agreed session and received three copper from labor funds. Yue placed the coins beside the first day's wage, then closed her purse before the account became the whole meaning of the afternoon.

season_garden_02_039.speaker: narrator
season_garden_02_039.text: A rain cloud crossed the bright doorway as they finished. The gardener checked the temporary protections and secured stored timber with the staff member responsible for the heavier work. Yue and Qiu returned their small tools, emptied only their assigned waste tray and left the uncertain plant material with its proper owner. They did not take specimens home for private experiments. The world beyond the gate contained plants they could admire without consuming the orchard's actual stock or extending its limited maintenance agreement.

season_garden_02_040.speaker: rival_qiu_zhen
season_garden_02_040.text: “I dislike how often you have a useful qualification,” Qiu said while they waited for the side entrance to clear. Yue asked whether she disliked the qualification or the delay in hearing the rest of the sentence. Qiu said both, depending on whether she had eaten. That made Yue laugh. The answer gave them a concrete condition instead of a fixed character judgment. They had disagreed less sharply after their break, and neither needed to turn that observation into a diagnosis of the other.

season_garden_02_041.speaker: lin_yue
season_garden_02_041.text: “I dislike how often your quick question reaches the thing somebody actually wants,” Yue answered. Qiu looked pleased until Yue added that she also disliked when speed made an unfinished condition sound already settled. “Fair,” Qiu said after a pause. They stood with the rain not yet falling and the doorway still occupied by a slow-moving visitor. Nobody asked the visitor to hurry so the practitioners could complete their agreeable exchange. Their own good conversation could wait while another person's feet found the step.

season_garden_02_042.speaker: narrator
season_garden_02_042.text: Su came outside after locking the work drawer. She asked the women whether they wanted the next-session reminder through the orchard's ordinary notice arrangement, with their choice of contact and no personal medical details included. Yue chose the written reminder at her existing agreed address. Qiu chose to check the posted board herself. Their differing arrangements would not be read as unequal commitment. If a notice changed, the staff would use the agreed method for each helper rather than assume every person watched the same doorway.

season_garden_02_043.speaker: narrator
season_garden_02_043.text: The pinwheel child called goodbye from inside the hall. His grandmother was resting, and he lowered his voice after his visiting adult reminded him. Qiu waved without stepping back into the room. Yue thought of how many departures she had once delayed by finding one more useful thing to do. This goodbye belonged at the gate. The child did not need her to remain until he became bored, and the orchard did not need her evening to prove the completed afternoon had mattered.

season_garden_02_044.speaker: narrator
season_garden_02_044.text: On the street, the rain finally began. Yue and Qiu separated at the ordinary fork their different routes required. Whatever relation their prior trial and present choices actually supported, both could leave without making the other explain the destination. Yue held her bag on the side that had worked safely that day and walked toward her own supper. The new garden work remained unfinished in specific ways, and more usable in specific ways. Those facts could stay at the orchard while she went home.

season_garden_02_priority_gate.speaker: narrator
season_garden_02_priority_gate.text: The first preparation could not be described until its actual selected priority was named. Su turned the shared sheet toward the responsible worker. Route border preparation and shelter seating preparation used different pieces, different checks and different handovers. The request postponed at the first choice retained its agreed next session. Yue waited for the worker's specific instruction rather than allowing her current preference to revise the choice quietly. Qiu put the gauge on the table, ready for whichever light assignment the saved selection supported.

season_garden_02_route_01.speaker: narrator
season_garden_02_route_01.text: The route border came first because that was the priority Yue had actually selected. The gardener had prepared sound light pieces in dimensions suitable for the permitted turn, and explained which edges the helpers could smooth without altering the join. Staff would reset the heavier bed frame. Yue took the nearest tray so she would not reach across her shoulder. Qiu laid her cord along the loose pieces, then removed it before a visitor could mistake the work area for a passage.

season_garden_02_route_02.speaker: rival_qiu_zhen
season_garden_02_route_02.text: “I measured the bed yesterday in my head,” Qiu admitted. “It was longer there.” She had imagined completing the first border in one clean sweep. The real turn had a slight widening where supported walkers needed room to change direction. The gardener demonstrated that width with the actual route plan rather than an invented average body. Qiu rechecked the pieces without cutting anything. A neat rectangle would have used less timber and given the wrong answer to the space people actually needed.

season_garden_02_route_03.speaker: narrator
season_garden_02_route_03.text: Yue worked on the light edge of one removable section while Qiu marked the corresponding orientation lines. Their separate tasks met at a handover they could inspect together. Qiu finished the marks quickly, then noticed that Yue had placed her section with the underside upward for a safer movement. She turned her own reference drawing rather than asking Yue to turn the work back. The adjustment cost seconds. It allowed the instruction and the worker's body to describe the same piece without either pretending not to matter.

season_garden_02_route_04.speaker: narrator
season_garden_02_route_04.text: The hand tool caught on a hard knot. Yue stopped before applying more force and called the gardener's maintenance worker. He checked the grain, chose another sound piece and retained the unsuitable one for a different approved use. She had neither failed the task nor secretly diagnosed timber through qi. Qiu wrote the substitution beside the section number. Her clear quick note would prevent the worker later looking for the rejected piece in the accepted stack. Here speed supported the pause instead of competing with it.

season_garden_02_route_05.speaker: lin_yue
season_garden_02_route_05.text: “I wanted to push once more,” Yue said after the worker moved away. “Only a little. I thought a small stop might become a large delay.” Qiu answered that she had been about to tell her the knot looked almost cleared. Both women had felt how an apparently tiny finish could make stopping embarrassing. They left the unsuitable timber where the worker had placed it. The delay belonged to discovering the actual material, not to Yue failing to perform the shape somebody had imagined before seeing it.

season_garden_02_route_06.speaker: narrator
season_garden_02_route_06.text: Their first prepared section was checked by the responsible worker and accepted for installation. The second needed a smoother exposed corner where clothing might catch. Qiu offered to complete that correction while Yue prepared the next light tray. Yue agreed because the motion suited Qiu's present limits and remained within their assignment. She did not pass the correction merely to hide it from her own report. Both helpers would name the change and its accepted check when they described what had actually been done.

season_garden_02_route_07.speaker: narrator
season_garden_02_route_07.text: When the staff reset the heavier frame, the helpers kept clear of the lifting line and used the time to sort the remaining pieces at their table. No qi gathered from their Four pairs supported the bed, restrained a damaged tree or powered the public route. The staff used rated ordinary tools and their own trained work. Yue watched the careful lowering and found it satisfying precisely because the completed weight had not become a test of her own shoulder. Somebody else's competence could be allowed to remain visible.

season_garden_02_route_08.speaker: narrator
season_garden_02_route_08.text: The gardener installed the accepted border sections after the heavier frame was secure, then checked the walking width and runoff before permitting ordinary use. The temporary boards remained where he still wanted them. The helpers did not declare the entire route open; the damaged upper path and fallen-tree area stayed closed. Qiu looked down the short turn they had improved. It was unremarkable enough that a visitor might never know how awkward it had been. She seemed both pleased and disappointed by that possibility.

season_garden_02_route_09.speaker: rival_qiu_zhen
season_garden_02_route_09.text: “If nobody notices, I will have to ask whether that means it works,” Qiu said. Yue answered that staff could observe whether soil still reached the route and users could describe their actual turn. Absence of complaint alone would not prove every person found it usable. Qiu nodded, then said she wanted at least one person to enjoy the improvement before it became another invisible obligation. Yue understood the wish. Their work could be quietly useful without requiring its makers to pretend they never wanted appreciation.

season_garden_02_route_10.speaker: narrator
season_garden_02_route_10.text: A visitor carrying a light basket passed along the checked short route. She did not stumble or perform a demonstration. At the turn she shifted the basket from one hand to the other and paused to greet the kitchen woman. Staff watched the space remain clear without interrupting her ordinary purpose. Yue noticed that the visitor had room to stop as well as move. A usable route was not merely a line drawn for continuous travel. It allowed a life to hesitate inside it without obstructing everybody behind.

season_garden_02_route_11.speaker: narrator
season_garden_02_route_11.text: The gardener asked them to leave the last prepared section uninstalled until the drainage could be checked after the next ordinary watering. Finishing its preparation did not entitle them to finish its placement. Qiu put it on the labeled safe shelf with the actual pending condition written beside it. Yue felt her own impatience rise at the missing final line. They had both done the selected task and left part of its future use waiting. The report needed room for that truthful untidy combination.

season_garden_02_route_12.speaker: narrator
season_garden_02_route_12.text: The bench owner passed on her way to the kitchen. She saw the improved turn and said it would make carrying soup easier when she came through. Yue told her the seating preparation retained its next agreed session and the carpenter's confirmed return. The woman said she knew, but had enjoyed being told without having to chase them. The unchosen request was still owned by somebody living a day beside the work. It deserved an answer more concrete than reassurance that the helpers remembered all important things.

season_garden_02_route_13.speaker: narrator
season_garden_02_route_13.text: Before their break, the helpers returned the accepted tools and washed their hands. Yue wrote the route's actual short improvement, the pending last section and the still-closed upper area in separate lines. Qiu checked the orientation marks against the worker's accepted pieces rather than against her earlier imagined rectangle. Their chosen priority had produced a real result with limits. They took those limits back to the shared table, where the rest of the afternoon had work that did not depend on calling the first result complete.

season_garden_02_seats_01.speaker: narrator
season_garden_02_seats_01.text: The shelter seating fittings came first because that was the priority Yue had actually selected. The carpenter had supplied light pieces from sound stock and demonstrated their permitted preparation at the work table. He would fit the structural rail, inspect the joints and test the assembled bench himself. Yue and Qiu could smooth approved exposed edges and mark orientation. The owner had requested safe retention of the worn seat and a separate keepsake from the old rail. Neither request made damaged timber trustworthy.

season_garden_02_seats_02.speaker: rival_qiu_zhen
season_garden_02_seats_02.text: “I pictured a bench before I pictured these twelve little pieces,” Qiu said. The carpenter explained which fittings helped locate the new rail and which merely finished an exposed surface. Their work was small enough to fit the available session, but it belonged to a larger repair whose order mattered. Qiu checked her gauge against his marked sample instead of declaring an improved design. Speed could save his preparation time if it preserved the actual fit. A faster wrong piece would only return as another delay.

season_garden_02_seats_03.speaker: narrator
season_garden_02_seats_03.text: Yue held the nearest removable piece on its supplied support and smoothed the exposed edge with the approved light motion. The carpenter checked her working position and confirmed that she did not need to press through a hard resistance. Qiu marked the corresponding pieces so staff could identify them without lifting every tray. Their separate tasks met at the table's center, where each accepted handover could be counted. The old bench waited out of use nearby, with a visible sign protecting it from hopeful early sitting.

season_garden_02_seats_04.speaker: narrator
season_garden_02_seats_04.text: One fitting had a slight warp. Qiu noticed it when her gauge would not sit as the marked sample had shown. She called the carpenter instead of shaving the piece until it resembled the desired reading. He checked the timber and supplied a sound replacement from existing stock. Qiu looked relieved and annoyed at once. A correction had made the repair safer and made her earlier neat stack less finished. Yue asked whether she wanted the rejected piece kept separate, and placed the labeled tray within easy reach.

season_garden_02_seats_05.speaker: lin_yue
season_garden_02_seats_05.text: “A surface can answer the gauge and still be the wrong piece,” Yue said. Qiu agreed without liking the general lesson being drawn from her particular correction. Yue caught that and returned to the actual timber. They recorded the replacement, the carpenter's check and the retained assignment. Nobody had lost a contest. The furniture needed a sound fitting, and they had helped discover which one failed that need. Their old rivalry could remain present without recruiting every small fault into an argument about a whole method.

season_garden_02_seats_06.speaker: narrator
season_garden_02_seats_06.text: The owner came to see the prepared pieces during a staff-approved pause in the work area. She ran her finger above the old seat without touching the carpenter's tools. The worn surface had a pale patch where her husband's sleeve used to brush it. She asked whether oiling would erase that patch. The carpenter explained the proposed finish and let her choose among safe suitable options. Yue and Qiu listened without making the owner's memory an obstacle to the fastest completion their hands could achieve.

season_garden_02_seats_07.speaker: narrator
season_garden_02_seats_07.text: The woman chose the finish that retained more of the visible wear while protecting the sound wood as the carpenter recommended. It would take its stated drying time before use. Qiu asked whether another safe seat could be placed nearby in the meantime, and staff confirmed the available indoor seating and the current outdoor chair arrangement. The remembered bench would not be used wet to make the afternoon feel complete. Its owner accepted that wait because somebody had answered where she could sit today.

season_garden_02_seats_08.speaker: narrator
season_garden_02_seats_08.text: A visiting adult asked whether the helpers could also repair a chair from her household. Su said this garden arrangement covered named communal maintenance, with its finite reserve and scheduled hours. The carpenter could consider a separate enquiry if he wished, but no absent future job was accepted on his behalf. The visitor took the ordinary contact information. Yue was glad that refusing an extra task did not require proving it unimportant. The household chair mattered to its owner and still lay outside this particular afternoon.

season_garden_02_seats_09.speaker: rival_qiu_zhen
season_garden_02_seats_09.text: “It is difficult to look useful without becoming available,” Qiu said after the visitor left. Yue answered that a clear yes might need an equally clear boundary around it. Qiu's expression suggested she disliked the elegance of that sentence. She preferred the work sheet's actual list: this bench, these fittings, this afternoon, this handover. Yue smiled and wrote the list beside the accepted pieces. Sometimes a rival's impatience with a fine phrase could save the phrase from replacing the work it claimed to explain.

season_garden_02_seats_10.speaker: narrator
season_garden_02_seats_10.text: The carpenter accepted the first tray and requested a correction to the final corner of one piece, where clothing might catch. Qiu completed it while Yue prepared the next tray within her comfortable reach. The correction stayed in the shared report. They were not submitting a perfect first attempt for a prize; they were making pieces a qualified worker could use. Their willingness to name the second pass would help him understand what had actually been changed before final fitting. Invisible correction could make visible completion harder to trust.

season_garden_02_seats_11.speaker: narrator
season_garden_02_seats_11.text: At the retained route turn, staff had kept the temporary protections sound and the walking width clear. The gardener reported that no new spill had altered the order agreed for the next session. Yue asked whether anyone had found the temporary turn unmanageable and received the current limited observations, not a claim about every possible visitor. The border request remained live. Choosing seating first had not settled it by making its users quieter, and the next afternoon's actual assignment still had to honor their passage.

season_garden_02_seats_12.speaker: narrator
season_garden_02_seats_12.text: Before the break, the carpenter set aside the accepted fittings for his confirmed return and showed both helpers which tray remained pending a final check. No repaired bench was yet available for use. The sign stayed on the furniture and the owner's separate rail stayed on her shelf. Qiu watched the tidy stack with the strange frustration of somebody whose useful work was complete while its desired result still belonged to another day. Yue understood the feeling and did not ask her to perform contentment.

season_garden_02_seats_13.speaker: narrator
season_garden_02_seats_13.text: They washed the timber dust from their fingers and returned to the shared table. Yue recorded the completed preparation, the correction and the carpenter's still-pending installation and load check. Qiu checked the actual piece count against the accepted trays, leaving out the rejected fitting. Their chosen priority had made the scheduled repair easier without producing a bench through narrative confidence. The rest of the afternoon offered other light work, while the unfinished result retained its real owner, date and conditions rather than following them into an unearned claim.
